newsitem.title: USA: Pol Pot should be tried internationally - Albright.
newsitem.headline: Pol Pot should be tried internationally - Albright.

text.p: The United States believes that captured Khmer Rouge strongman Pol Pot should face international justice and is discussing the issue with its allies, Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Sunday.

Interviewed at the Group of Seven summit here by ABC's "This Week," Albright said that if the reports of Pol Pot's capture were correct, "we will be seeking to make sure that there is international justice carried out against this major war criminal."

Albright did not elaborate but she added that the issue of what should be done with the man responsible for the genocide of more than one million Cambodians after the 1975 communist takeover was discussed by the eight nations attending the Denver summit.

"This was a subject of discussion here in Denver...about what kind of international approach should be taken...These are things we have to determine, but it clearly is an international issue," she said.

Albright will make a previously scheduled visit to Cambodia and Vietnam this week on her way to Hong Kong to attend ceremonies marking China's takeover of the British colony. She said the United States was carefully monitoring the Hong Kong transfer.

"The issue here though of course is not so much what happens on that one day but what happens in the long run in Hong Kong...We are going to watch it very carefully and we will determine our relationship according to that as a test -- how it will work," she said.
The Cambodian government has said it asked the United Nations for help to bring Pol Pot before an international tribunal.
More than one million people were executed as enemies of Pol Pot's utopian revolution or died of disease, starvation or overwork during the Khmer Rouge's 1975-79 rule.
A senior Cambodian military officer said Pol Pot was being held in the jungle village headquarters of a breakaway Khmer Rouge faction and would be transferred to Phom Penh.
Nhiek Bun Chhay, Cambodia's armed forces' deputy chief of general staff, said he saw Pol Pot under arrest in the village of Anlong Veng and that he would be handed over to the government soon.
